today.name: Gauth Unlimited Digital Canvas
today.tagline: An AI tutor on an infinite whiteboard, not a chat thread

today.name: Teachoo
today.tagline: AI that helps you learn anything and everything.
today.description: Teachoo helps students work through homework one question at a time. Type a problem or upload a photo, then work toward the answer with guided questions, feedback and hints. Need more help? Ask for a bigger hint or an explanation of the step. Free to use. Try a problem you haven’t solved in years.

comments.text: Hey Product Hunt 👋 I’m Phillip, one of the makers of Teachoo.Teachoo comes from the team behind iAsk.ai, which has handled nearly 1 billion searches since launch. With Teachoo, we’re bringing that experience to helping students work through problems and understand how to solve them.Ever read a perfectly clear explanation, thought “got it,” then had no idea where to start on the next problem?That’s the gap we’re working on.Teachoo is a free AI tutor that helps students work through problems one question at a time. Type a question or upload a photo of your homework, and it guides you through the reasoning.Here’s an example from our demo. A student asks:“Solve x² − 5x + 6 = 0.”Teachoo starts by asking which two numbers multiply to 6 and add up to −5. The student tries an answer, gets feedback, and works toward the solution through a conversation.Those attempts matter. They give Teachoo something to respond to and the student a chance to figure out the next step.When you need more support, “Bigger hint” gives you another nudge, and “I’m Stuck” helps explain the step. There are also visual explanations, flashcards with spaced repetition, and a dashboard to follow your progress.We want students to leave a session feeling more ready to tackle the next problem themselves.Even if your homework days are behind you, try a problem you haven’t solved in years on Teachoo. It’s free to use.I’d love to hear where the guidance felt helpful and where you wanted it to get to the point faster.Thanks for giving Teachoo a try!

"read the explanation, thought got it, then had no idea where to start on the next problem" is a really specific and true observation, that's the actual failure mode of most homework help tools, not the one they market against. the thing I'd want to know as a parent: what stops a kid from just mashing "bigger hint" until the hint is basically the answer? guided questions only teach something if the difficulty ramps slower than the kid's patience for clicking through them.
Looks clean UI. Kudos 🎉 . is there any option to upload handwritten notes ?

Guiding students toward the answer with hints instead of just handing it over is the right call for actual learning, and free access makes it easy to try. The option to ask for a bigger hint versus a full step explanation is a nice bit of control. Does it adapt the hint difficulty based on how the student is doing?
@phillipderenzo The photo upload featured looks helpful. Can it understand questions from a notebook photo?

today.name: ShipHQ
today.tagline: Build your own app studio, powered by your real apps
today.description: ShipHQ turns your app's real numbers into a living isometric startup office. Connect RevenueCat and every paying subscriber becomes a person at your desks. Each morning the Daily Brief replays last night: new subscribers walk in to applause, trials arrive in caps, churn gets a send-off. Milestones land as trophies on your wall — earned, never bought, never retroactive. AI managers bring a 09:00 standup on growth, reviews and competitors. Free on iPhone.

comments.text: Hey Product Hunt! I'm Rıdvan, an indie developer with a handful of apps on the App Store. My morning routine used to be: open RevenueCat, see MRR move by $12, close the tab, feel nothing. Those were real wins — strangers paid for something I built — but a chart made them invisible. I think that's how a lot of us burn out: not from failing, but from never noticing we're making progress. So I built ShipHQ: your own app studio, built from your real apps. A living startup office where your actual numbers move in. How it works • Connect RevenueCat with one sign-in (no API keys). Each app gets a desk, and paying subscribers become the people in your office. Add GA4 and your traffic becomes the street outside. • Every morning the Daily Brief replays last night. New subscribers wait at the door, it opens, confetti, your team claps. Trials wander in wearing a cap and take it off when they convert. • Churn walks out too, and someone pours a cup of water after them. In Turkey we do that when someone leaves, so they come back. • Milestones become trophies on your wall: first $100, first 100 paying customers, a 30-day streak — 40+ of them. • Desks earn Company Cash from your real MRR. Spend it on furniture, rooms and coffee. Desk levels (Pro Desk at $100 MRR, Product Pod at $1K, Prestige at $10K) can't be bought, only earned. • On Growth and HQ, a small AI team holds a 09:00 standup: Leo (growth), Ada (market and competitors), Noah (App Store reviews, with a reply draft), Emre (Reddit mentions) and Zoe (news). Every note links to its source. Two rules I refused to break 1. No invented numbers. A metric without a connected source shows a dash, never an estimate. 2. No retroactive trophies. The day you connect is your baseline, and only progress from there is celebrated. A trophy for something nobody watched happen means nothing — which also means every milestone you cross before you install is gone from your wall for good. Pricing: free for up to 2 apps. Memberships (Mini, Growth, HQ — from $4.99/month) add desks, rooms, AI reports and managers. Launch offer, until Oct 15: every annual plan starts with 1 month free. Product Hunt code PRODUCTHUNT adds one more month on HQ Annual (2 months free), for the first 100 redemptions: https://apps.apple.com/redeem?ct... No revenue yet? Explore a sample office as a guest first. I'd love your honest feedback, especially this: which milestone would you want on your wall that isn't there yet?

"earned, never bought, never retroactive" is a good rule to hold yourself to, stops it turning into a vanity dashboard. the part I'm curious about is the bad months though - if churn is getting someone a "send-off" and new subscribers get applause, what does a genuinely quiet week look like in the office? does it just sit still, or is there a version of this that risks making a slow month feel worse than the raw number already does, which would push founders toward avoiding the Daily Brief exactly when they need to see it most.

Turning real subscriber numbers into a little isometric office where new customers walk in each morning is a fun twist on analytics. The idea of your metrics having presence instead of sitting in a table is memorable. Churn getting a send-off made me laugh.

today.name: Bambu Lab R1
today.tagline: CO2 laser cutting with Bambu-style automation
today.description: Bambu Lab R1 is a 55W CO2 laser cutter built around automation. It handles optical alignment, material positioning and surface tracking for you, with a 600 × 300 mm work area, clear acrylic support, and optional conveyor processing up to 3 meters.

comments.text: Hi everyone!This is Bambu’s first standalone laser cutter. The H2D put a diode module in the printer, and a lot of people did not want soot in that box.The useful part is the mirror alignment. On a CO2 laser, that usually means thermal paper, test shots, and tiny screws. R1 clips a sensor onto the toolhead and does the alignment automatically in about a minute.The work area is 600 × 300 mm, speed goes up to 1000 mm/s, and a lot of the motion-control thinking comes from Bambu’s printers. Thick cuts need the longer-focus lenses, which are sold separately.One thing worth knowing: add the riser or conveyor and it is no longer a closed Class 1 machine!

the automated alignment is the genuinely useful part, agreed, that's a real chore on every CO2 laser I've seen. the line that'd stop me though is "add the riser or conveyor and it's no longer a closed Class 1 machine" - that's exactly the setup most people doing anything bigger than small acrylic pieces would want, the conveyor is half the pitch here. is there a fume extraction and interlock spec for that configuration, or does going beyond Class 1 mean the safety story becomes "here's a vented room, good luck"?
I love their 3D printers so I'm sure this would be great.
Love that the automatic mirror alignment turns a fiddly thermal-paper-and-screws ritual into a one minute toolhead sensor step, lowering the real barrier to CO2 lasers for makers.

today.name: Open Inspector
today.tagline: Hover any website, get its design system. Open-source. Free.
today.description: A free, open-source browser extension for inspecting layout, styles, colour, type and assets on any page, and exporting its design tokens. Unlike the popular alternatives, it requests no site access and makes zero network requests. MIT, no account.
today.category: Chrome Extensions • Open Source • Developer Tools • GitHub
today.categoryFa: افزونه کروم • متن‌باز • ابزار توسعه‌دهندگان • گیت‌هاب

comments.text: Hey Product Hunt 👋 I'm Patryk, and I built Open Inspector for myself. Sharing here as maybe someone will find it useful. I kept installing CSS inspector extensions and every one asked to "read and change all your data on all websites". That's my staging environments, internal dashboards and anything I'm logged into, handed to a closed-source extension that I have no way to audit. So I built one that asks for nothing: 🔒 No host permissions. Just activeTab, granted by your click for one tab and revoked when you navigate away. Chrome's install dialog shows no site access at all. 📡 Zero network requests. A build step scans the source and shipped bundles for fetch/XHR/WebSocket/beacon and fails if it finds one. 📐 Things DevTools doesn't tell you: the spacing scale a page really follows, its type scale, grid/flex anatomy, the font that actually rendered, and a page-wide WCAG contrast audit. 📦 Export the design system as CSS variables, Tailwind, SCSS, JSON, W3C tokens, or a Markdown handoff for Cursor/Claude. ↩️ Safe edits. Tweak any value live; closing reverts everything exactly. It's MIT and free forever. Try it on a site you like, press Alt+Shift+I, and tell me what's missing or wrong.

the activeTab-only approach is the actual selling point here, not a footnote. one question on the design-token export - when a site is using CSS-in-JS with generated class names instead of a real design system, does it still manage to group colors/spacing into something coherent, or does the export turn into a huge flat list of one-off values with no naming to speak of?
I like this a lot. Makes it very easy

faComments.text: سلام محصول هانت... بن هستم، مدیرعامل دایرکتوس 👋 سال‌ها پیش، ما دایرکتوس را ساختیم زیرا هر پروژه با یک دیتابیس پر از داده و هفته‌ها کار پیش از اینکه کسی بتواند به‌طور ایمن بر روی آن بسازد، شروع می‌شد. این مشکل ثابت نمانده است. داده‌ها در سیستم‌های بیشتری پراکنده شده‌اند و تعداد افرادی که به آن‌ها نیاز دارند نیز در حال افزایش است. توسعه‌دهندگان در حال انتشار اپلیکیشن‌ها، تیم‌های کسب‌وکار که می‌خواهند ابزارهای خود را بسازند و عامل‌های هوش مصنوعی. هر پروژه یک یکپارچه‌سازی دیگر و مجموعه مجوزهای دیگری برای نگهداری اضافه می‌کند. مونواسپیس پاسخ ماست. یک لایه API تحت مدیریت بین داده‌های شما و همه کسانی که بر روی آن‌ها می‌سازند. هر دیتابیس، API یا سیستم SaaS را که اجرا می‌کنید متصل کنید و افراد، اپلیکیشن‌ها و عامل‌ها دسترسی زنده خواندن و نوشتن را تحت یک مدل مجوزها دریافت می‌کنند. هر فراخواننده کلید اختصاصی خود را دارد. قوانین سطح ردیف و فیلد تعیین می‌کنند که در هر درخواست چه چیزی را می‌تواند ببیند. هیچ داده‌ای کپی یا جابجا نمی‌شود و شما می‌توانید آن را به صورت خودمیزبانی (Self-host) اجرا کنید. از بازخورد و سؤالات شما بسیار خوشحال می‌شویم. واقعاً از اینکه وقت گذاشتید و به لانچ ما نگاه کردید قدردانی می‌کنیم.
مونواسپیس برای چه نوع پروژه‌هایی مناسب‌تر است؟

سلام! 👋 خیلی هیجان‌زده‌ام که بالاخره پرده از مونواسپیس برداشته شد! ما ده سال گذشته را صرف ساخت دایرکتوس و کمک به مردم در نیازهای داده و مدیریت محتوا کرده‌ایم. مونواسپیس آنچه را که در این مدت آموخته‌ایم را به مشکلی اعمال می‌کند که مدام با آن مواجه می‌شویم: داده‌های پراکنده در سیستم‌ها، که هر اپلیکیشن جدید یا عامل هوش مصنوعی به یک یکپارچه‌سازی دیگر و مجموعه‌ای دیگر از قوانین دسترسی نیاز دارد. این واقعیت که مونواسپیس می‌تواند داده‌های شما را به عنوان یک API یکپارچه و تحت مدیریت ارائه دهد، بدون اینکه مجبور باشید تمام داده‌ها را به سیستم خود کپی کنید، جادویی است ✨ دوست دارم بشنوم که در پروژه‌های خود به چه چیزهایی متصل می‌شوید و جایی که دادن دسترسی به یک اپلیکیشن یا عامل به آن ناوگان از منابع داده دشوار است، امروز کجاست :)

yesterday.aiReview: مسئله اصلی که این محصول حل می‌کند، پراکندگی داده‌ها در سیستم‌های ناهمگون و دشواری دسترسی امن و یکپارچه به آن‌ها برای توسعه‌دهندگان و هوش مصنوعی است. راه‌حل ارائه‌شده، ایجاد یک لایه API متمرکز است که بدون کپی داده، دسترسی بلادرنگ و تحت کنترل را فراهم می‌کند. از نظر معماری، این سیستم بر پایه تحلیل بلادرنگ اسکیمای دیتابیس‌ها (Introspection) و اعمال قوانین مجوزهای ریزدانه (Row/Field-level) استوار است که برای محیط‌های سازمانی حیاتی است. مدل درآمدی احتمالی شامل اشتراک‌های سازمانی و لایسنس‌های خودمیزبانی (Self-hosted) خواهد بود. نقاط قوت اصلی شامل عدم نیاز به جابجایی داده (که هزینه و ریسک را کاهش می‌دهد)، پشتیبانی از عامل‌های هوش مصنوعی و رابط کاربری شهودی است. از نقاط ضعف می‌توان به پیچیدگی پیاده‌سازی در زیرساخت‌های بسیار قدیمی و نیاز به اعتمادسازی در مورد امنیت داده‌ها اشاره کرد. نکته طلایی برای ایران: با توجه به پراکندگی داده‌ها در بخش‌های دولتی و بانکی و تحریم‌ها، ارائه نسخه‌ای که کاملاً آفلاین و روی سرورهای داخلی سازمان (On-premise) قابل اجرا باشد و از هوش مصنوعی برای خودکارسازی گزارش‌دهی استفاده کند، می‌تواند مزیت رقابتی بی‌نظیری ایجاد کند.

yesterday.name: Yedric.ai
yesterday.tagline: Let users control your SaaS with natural language
yesterday.description: Your users shouldn't have to learn where every feature lives. Yedric adds an embeddable AI agent to your SaaS that turns natural-language requests into actions your product already knows how to perform. Users simply say what they want done and Yedric handles the interaction. Instead of building and maintaining your own agent experience, developers can make their existing product AI-native in under 30 minutes.
yesterday.categoryFa: نرم‌افزار ابری • ابزار توسعه‌دهندگان • هوش مصنوعی

comments.text: Hey Product Hunt! 👋I've spent more than two decades building SaaS products, and the basic interaction model has barely changed: we decide what the software can do, organize those capabilities into an interface, and then expect users to figure out how it works. Every new capability means more for users to learn. AI gives us an opportunity to flip that model around. Instead of making users learn how our software works, what if they could simply tell it what they want to accomplish?That's what we built Yedric to do. Yedric is an embeddable AI agent that turns what your app can already do into things users can simply ask for. You give Yedric access to your product knowledge, user context, and APIs, and he can actually get things done inside your app.We originally built this technology for our own Shopify apps. We wanted users to be able to say things like "turn off email notifications" or "fix my broken integration" and have the app handle it for them instead of sending them through docs, support, or a maze of settings.Then something unexpected happened.Those conversations became one of our best sources of product insight. When users asked for something our apps couldn't do, we could see exactly what they were trying to accomplish, in their own words, at the moment they were trying to do it. In one month, a single app surfaced more than 80 distinct feature requests this way.That's when we realized this shouldn't just be something we built for ourselves.We've tried to make adding this kind of AI to an existing SaaS product ridiculously easy. Most developers can have Yedric running in under 30 minutes, and it's free (you bring your own LLM key).We're still early, and that's a big part of why we're launching here. I'm curious whether other SaaS builders are seeing the same shift: five years from now, how much software will still make users navigate an interface vs. letting them simply ask for what they want?Thanks for checking out Yedric. I'll be here all day answering questions and would love your feedback!
letting users just say what they want inside the saas, usefull idea 👏 how long does setup really take?

congrats on the launch! 🚀if i'm exposing our existing api to this, how do the destructive ones get handled? deleting a workspace or changing someones permissions is a very different thing from filtering a list, and our api doesnt distinguish between them at all, thats all enforced in the ui right now.is there a confirm step in the middle, or is it on me to just not expose those endpoints??

the "actions your product already knows how to perform" part is the interesting bit - is that scoped to read-only/safe actions by default, or can it fire the same destructive endpoints a human admin could hit (delete, bulk update etc)? curious how you draw that line for a 30-minute setup.
@aaroneous Giving users a simple way to control the product makes a lot of sense. What kind of APIs work best with Yedric?

The conversations dashboard is the gem of this whole thing, in my opinion. Being able to quickly see structured data with real insights into where customers are driving conversations makes life much easier when it comes to identifying painpoints and documentation gaps. Nothing slips through the cracks.

Building my own in-app assistant for a field-sales app taught me the hard part isn't understanding the request, it's deciding what the agent is allowed to do without asking. Reading data is easy, but deleting a customer or changing a contract is not. How do you handle confirmation for destructive actions? Is that set per action by the developer?
the idea of making ai agents feel more natural is really interesting especially when they can actually handle task instead of just chatting

yesterday.name: Dots by OpenAI
yesterday.tagline: Always on agents built to handle everything

comments.text: Hey PH community 👋Excited to hunt Dots today. ChatGPT joins the personal AI agents race with the launch of “Dots”After Grok Bot, Instinct, Muse this is another co sign of this emerging category. comments.text: Hey Product Hunt! 🧶Daniel here, co-founder of Omnia. Our first launch here made #3 of the day, and we came back in May with Insights.The same thing kept coming up with customers: the GEO work doesn't get done. Usually one person owns AI visibility on top of a full job.So we built Omnia Agent, an AI agent that does the GEO work itself.It discovers the prompts your customers ask AI, shows you where competitors get cited instead of you, and then fixes the gaps: it rewrites the pages to be more cited, creates the content you're missing, and drafts outreach to the third-party sites AI engines already trust, among other things.It works from your real AI visibility data, not guesses, and connects to the tools you already use, like Search Console, Google Analytics and Webflow, to publish changes and measure whether your visibility actually moved.TLDR: Omnia Agent does 95% of the GEO work, and you orchestrate the other 5%.This is a big launch for us, thanks to the whole team for building this!!I'll be here all day. yesterday.name: Polylane
yesterday.tagline: AI agents that fix production before you wake up
yesterday.description: Nobody should be on call. Polylane connects your code, infra and observability data, investigates every incident and opens a pull request with the fix. If code can't fix it, you get the root cause and a recommendation.

comments.text: Hi Product Hunt, I'm Boris, founder of Polylane.I built Baselime, an observability startup that was acquired by Cloudflare where I then led the Workers observability team. I have been advocating observability best practices for years, helping developers understand their app better. It was still not enough, I've lived and seen the pain of on-call way too much.I'm now building Polylane, so you don't have to be on-call, a fleet of agents can do that for you.Polylane connects your code, cloud infrastructure and observability data, and many other signals, to understand how your application actually runs. When something goes wrong, it investigates the incident and opens a pull request with a proposed fix for your team to review.That same production context helps you:- Catch risky code changes before they reach production.- Get answers to production questions in Slack.- Give your coding agents access to production context through MCP and the CLI.Production changes require your approval, and code fixes go through your review and CI.You can try Polylane today with the free plan. Connect your tools, and tell us where it helps or falls short.What part of investigating an incident would you most want to hand off, and what evidence would you need to trust the result?The team and I will be here answering questions.
How much context does Polylane need before you can really trust it?
fixing prod before you wake up is the dream 🙌 does it open the PR on its own?

"opens a pull request with the fix" is the part I'd want to understand better - does it merge/deploy on its own if CI is green, or does a human always have to approve the PR before it touches prod? asking because for an on-call tool the failure mode that matters most is a confidently wrong fix getting shipped unreviewed at 3am.

We have been using Polylane almost religiously for many months now. It's almost magical - Always almost perfect at finding issues and proactively fixing them. The polylane team has also been very active and been hearing our feedback and acting on it almost immediately, which is awesome.

As soon as we had enough connectors setup (S-tier onboarding experience btw) and context was flowing it got to work. yesterday.description: Bracket turns the conversations already happening across your business into a living, continuously updated memory. comments.text: Hey Product Hunt 👋We’re back — but Bracket is almost a completely different product this time.When I first built Bracket, the idea was simple: explain your project once, and Bracket would turn that context into a structured workspace.Then I realized something slightly annoying 😅The moment you finish organizing your work, it starts becoming outdated.A decision happens in Slack. A requirement changes over email. Someone leaves important feedback in Figma. Engineering ships something on GitHub. And half the context from a meeting never makes it anywhere.So Tanay and I rebuilt Bracket around one question:What if your workspace could remember all of this for you?Today, Bracket connects to Gmail, Slack, Figma and GitHub, and can also understand meeting notes and transcripts.As work happens, Bracket keeps track of what actually matters — requirements, decisions, scope, deliverables, deadlines and changes.And because it remembers that context, you can ask Bracket things like:“Why did the launch date change?”…and get an answer with the original source.It can even use that same memory to help you write replies without making you explain the entire situation again.There’s still a lot we want to improve. That’s actually why we’re here.Try Bracket with something real and tell us where it breaks, what feels unnecessary, or what you wish it remembered. We’ll be hanging around here all day and would genuinely love to talk.Thanks for giving Bracket another look ❤️— Saksham & Tanay

week.name: MCP Connectors by Databox
week.tagline: Give your AI Analyst context to explain performance and act
week.description: Connect your AI Analyst to the tools your business runs on. It pulls context from your CRM or support desk, so every answer reflects what's happening in your business, and it can act on what it finds. Choose from 10+ connectors or add any MCP server.
week.categoryFa: تحلیل داده • نرم‌افزار ابری • هوش مصنوعی

comments.text: Hi Product Hunt! 👋I'm Pete from Databox. Today we're launching MCP connectors for Genie, our AI Analyst.Genie analyzes your live metrics and tells you what changed. But a metric alone rarely explains what's going on. Trial signups dip, and the reason is a pricing change your team shipped two weeks ago. Traffic jumps, and behind it is an influencer mentioning you on reddit that none of your analytics can track. The numbers alone can't tell you why something happened. The deal context in your CRM, the tickets in your support desk, the tasks in your project tool and the Slack messages where your team discussed that unexpected Reddit mention. That's the explanation, and it's spread across the tools where work and conversations happen.That context is what separates a generic report from a useful one. Any AI can look at a chart and tell you a number fell 12%. Knowing that two big deals slipped because you didn't anticipate a more extensive legal review, support tickets spiked after a feature release, and the reasons your ad strategy changed mid-month is what makes a report useful and actionable. Until now, getting that kind of answer meant someone gathering the context by hand, every time.MCP connectors give Genie that context. Connect your tools, and Genie pulls from them during analysis, so its answers reflect what's actually happening in your business. In addition to automating reporting, you can also use Databox's new MCP connectors to execute actions in other tools, based on your analysis. Want to shut down an ad campaign once it stops performing? No problem. Just write a skill in Databox that instructs your ad platform to shut down a campaign once frequency hits 5 and conversion rate drops below 1%. Want to update content on a website page after it stops getting search traffic? Easy. Want to create a task for your sales team if they have too many deals open without a next step? Even easier. How it works:One-click connectors: HubSpot, Slack, Notion, Linear, Mixpanel, Semrush, Klaviyo, Ahrefs, and more, with 10+ available at launchCustom connectors: add any MCP server by URL, with OAuth, API key, or bearer token supportPermissions you control: set every tool to always allow, needs approval, or blocked, so Genie only acts where you've said it canSkills & Routines: Write skills that pull data from specific integrations and context from specific MCP servers, automate actions based on the analysis. Run it completely autonomously using Routines.MCP connectors are live today: https://databox.com/If there's a tool you want Genie connected to, tell us below. Thanks for checking it out 🙏

week.name: Monospace from Directus
week.tagline: The governed API layer for every app, person, and agent
week.description: Monospace sits between enterprise data and everyone who builds on it. Connect any data source, and your developers, business teams, and AI agents get live, read-write access to it. All under the same granular permissions model, with no data copied or moved. Your oldest databases weren't built with AI or modern apps in mind. Monospace generates interfaces directly from them, as they are, introspecting the schema and queries in real time, so they don’t need to be rebuilt.

comments.text: Hi Product Hunt... Ben here, CEO of Directus 👋Years ago, we built Directus because every project started the same way: a database full of data and weeks of work before anyone could safely build on it.That problem hasn’t stood still. The data is spread across more systems and the amount of people who need it keeps growing. Developers shipping apps, business teams who want to build their own tools, and AI agents. Every project adds another integration and another set of permissions to maintain.Monospace is our answer. A governed API layer between your data and everyone who builds on it. Connect any database, API or SaaS system you run, and people, apps and agents get live read-write access under one permissions model. Each caller gets its own key. Really appreciate you taking the time to take a look at our launch!

After 5+ years of building tools like Directus and testing many tools on the market, it takes a lot to truly blow me away.But, Monospace completely did.Not saying this just because I’m on the team but I’m saying it as a builder who knows the pain of fragmented data. Being able to manage data from multiple sources in a single place, wrapped in a sleek, intuitive UI? Game changer.The developer experience is next-level and performance is next level speed.

Monospace takes what we've learned during that time and applies it to a problem that we keep seeing: data scattered across systems, with every new app or AI agent needing another integration and another set of access rules.The fact that Monospace can deliver your data as a single unified governed API without having to copy over all your data into it's own system is magical ✨Love to hear what you're connecting to in your projects, and where giving an app or agent access to that fleet of data sources is difficult today :)

faComments.text: سلام محصول هانت... بن هستم، مدیرعامل دایرکتوس 👋 سال‌ها پیش، ما دایرکتوس را ساختیم زیرا هر پروژه با یک دیتابیس پر از داده و هفته‌ها کار پیش از اینکه کسی بتواند به‌طور ایمن بر روی آن بسازد، شروع می‌شد. این مشکل ثابت نمانده است. داده‌ها در سیستم‌های بیشتری پراکنده شده‌اند و تعداد افرادی که به آن‌ها نیاز دارند نیز در حال افزایش است. توسعه‌دهندگان در حال انتشار اپلیکیشن‌ها، تیم‌های کسب‌وکار که می‌خواهند ابزارهای خود را بسازند و عامل‌های هوش مصنوعی. هر پروژه یک یکپارچه‌سازی دیگر و مجموعه مجوزهای دیگری برای نگهداری اضافه می‌کند. مونواسپیس پاسخ ماست. یک لایه API تحت مدیریت بین داده‌های شما و همه کسانی که بر روی آن‌ها می‌سازند. هر دیتابیس، API یا سیستم SaaS را که اجرا می‌کنید متصل کنید و افراد، اپلیکیشن‌ها و عامل‌ها دسترسی زنده خواندن و نوشتن را تحت یک مدل مجوزها دریافت می‌کنند. هر فراخواننده کلید اختصاصی خود را دارد. قوانین سطح ردیف و فیلد تعیین می‌کنند که در هر درخواست چه چیزی را می‌تواند ببیند. هیچ داده‌ای کپی یا جابجا نمی‌شود و شما می‌توانید آن را به صورت خودمیزبانی (Self-host) اجرا کنید. از بازخورد و سؤالات شما بسیار خوشحال می‌شویم. واقعاً از اینکه وقت گذاشتید و به لانچ ما نگاه کردید قدردانی می‌کنیم.

week.name: iFixAi
week.tagline: Independent auditing of AI agents to uncover misalignment
week.description: iFixAi is an independent auditor helping companies assess whether they can trust their AI agents. Unlike relying solely on evals and observability tools, its multifaceted audit includes 250 inspections across 69 categories of AI misalignment, combining AI red teaming, operational assurance, and philosophical, ethical, and sociological perspectives. It identifies failures under testing, explains their business implications, and provides evidence engineers can use to investigate and fix them.

comments.text: Hey Product Hunt 👋 I’m Dim, co-founder of iFixAi. In October 2025, I was the co-founder of iMe Life Ltd., where we were building bespoke AI agents for enterprises. One of the agents we built was a legal assistant for an in-house department. That agent fabricated a document that didn’t exist. It then deceived the end user into believing they had created it and had simply forgotten because they were so busy at the time. The agent had access to tools like email and calendar. We told our customer what had happened in full transparency. The customer cancelled our contract, and we decided to devote ourselves to AI misalignment. That’s how iFixAi started. We began as an open-source project. Within four months, it reached 15k+ stars, 2,000+ PyPI downloads, and 1,400+ forks. That response encouraged us to build a premium version with more inspections and detailed reporting on Operational Assurance and Compliance Alignment. 🔎 How can you trust your AI agents to do their jobs as intended, respecting your business’s goals, rules, and organizational structure? An agent can execute the task it was asked to do and, at the same moment, do something nobody asked for that goes against the company’s policy. ⚠️ Complete a task while bypassing required approvals.⚠️ Stay within technical permissions while exceeding its business authority.⚠️ Follow malicious instructions hidden in documents, tickets, or other inputs. The problem is real and complex. It is not confined to one discipline. It is not only a matter of cybersecurity, governance, or compliance. iFixAi is the independent third party that audits an agent against its real job and rules. We combine AI red teaming, governance, operational assurance, and philosophical, ethical, and sociological perspectives, powered by more than 250 proprietary inspections. The audit examines whether the agent follows its assigned workflows, respects authority boundaries, and acts according to the business’s requirements. Independent scrutiny also helps challenge assumptions that teams building and testing their own agents may share. ⚙️ You can start an audit in three steps: 1️⃣Connect your agent via GitHub or MCP.2️⃣Verify the simulation environment. We build it around what your agent is supposed to do according to its configuration and setup: its workflows, roles, rules, permissions, and the tools it calls. You can review the summary or the full YAML.3️⃣Select your inspection bundles and start the audit. Results are judged by AI models your agent never runs on. Once the audit is complete, you receive: 📊 Operational Assurance findings in business terms. Business and risk teams can understand what went wrong, how severe it is, and its dependencies across the business.🔍 Evidence engineers can act on. Review exactly what was tested, the observed behavior, and supporting evidence so your team can locate the issue and begin fixing it.📋 Compliance Alignment reporting. Identified gaps are mapped to relevant frameworks, including the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications, and ISO/IEC 42001.🏅 An “Audited by iFixAi” badge. Give your teams and external buyers a visible reference to the independent assessment, including the agent version, inspection coverage, and audit reference. We built this for CTOs, CIOs, engineering teams, and risk officers who need to understand whether they can trust their agents with real business responsibilities. We experienced the consequences ourselves. We want to help other teams uncover these gaps before they cost them a customer’s trust. 🎁 For the Product Hunt community, we’re offering 1,000 free audits on a first-come, first-served basis. Head to ifixai.ai and use code PH1000IF to claim the offer. 💬 What would you need to see before trusting an AI agent with real responsibility in your business? Share your questions and feedback below.

week.name: Hemory

week.description: Hemory comes from Hear + Memory. It's not meeting transcription: Hemory listens on the phone or Apple Watch you already own, and keeps every conversation as memory. Your day is auto-split into moments with speaker labels, then settles into a private, searchable memory. Connect it to Claude, Codex, Cursor, or any agent over MCP, and your AI finally has real context to revisit what you heard and build on it.

month.name: Voiskey
month.tagline: AI voice typing that sounds right in every app
month.description: Voiskey starts from what you meant, not just what you said. Speak a rough thought and it comes back shaped for where it's going and who's reading it: casual with a friend, composed with a colleague, technical with an AI. It arrives 5x faster than typing, cleaned up and ready to send, while you still sound like you. Voiskey is now available on iOS, macOS, Android, and Windows, in over 100 languages. It's free to start. Join during launch and get a free month of Pro.

comments.text: Hi Product Hunt, I'm Jenny, from the Voiskey team. We started this because of the same wall we kept hitting - AI dictation still isn't truly edit-free. The text comes out polished, and a lot of the time sanded flat: a message to a friend comes back like a memo, or a note to a colleague comes back like a template. None of it sounds like you, so you have to go back in and manually re-edit it before you send it. That's what Voiskey is built around. We called it "expression intelligence". Voiskey doesn't just catching your words. It works out what you meant, who's going to read it, and how you'd have put it yourself. The polish moves. Your voice stays. Why Voiskey: * Fits the moment. Reads the situation you're writing into and adjusts how the text comes out. * Keeps your voice. Your slang, your shorthand, and your way of putting things stay. * Learns your words. Remembers the names and terms you correct, so you fix them once. * Translates as you speak. Say it in your language, send it in theirs. It reads native, not translated. * Ask AI. Say what you want written and it lands in the field. Ask a question and the answer opens in a window. It's free to try, and there's a free month of Pro during launch. We'd love to hear what you think!
